# Quantum Training Robustness

> Companion repository for Probe Geometry and the Cost of Quantum Gate Certification.

The project answers Mayer and Knill's question about which identifying pure-state menus give linear control of gate infidelity. It also gives the sharp linear coefficient, bounds it at fixed menu size, and determines the optimal leading certification cost with fresh classically selected inputs. The target is unitary. The general theorems cover arbitrary CPTP implementations, with additional results for unital and exact product channels.

## Entry points

- [README](README.md): Main question, results, scope, purpose, and contact.
- [Scientific map](science/README.md): Reading routes, notation, and the correspondence to the manuscript's four theorems, corollary, and proposition.
- [Interpretation](science/interpretation.md): Consequences for training, physical promises, and resource accounting.

## Learning route

Follow the milestones for the guided route from the qubit example to the certification bounds. Use the scientific map for proofs and attribution.

The single educational anchor is John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018). Section pointers use the author's standard-layout pre-publication version. Research papers cited for attribution are not additional educational anchors.

- [Watrous bridge](learning/WATROUS_BRIDGE.md): Source sections, convention translations, and the missing connections from foundations to this project.
- [Thirty milestones](learning/MILESTONES.md): Common understanding map with 13 background/preliminaries and 17 narrative/innovation milestones, central questions, targets, dependencies, connections, and sources.
- [Fidelity and notation](learning/WATROUS_BRIDGE.md#notation): Root versus squared fidelity, Haar versus entanglement infidelity, and vectorization order.
- [Physical example](learning/WATROUS_BRIDGE.md#hidden-noise): Why two qubit probes can hide dissipation and a third detects it.
- [General certification](learning/MILESTONES.md#m23): M23–M26 connect the simultaneous adversary, adaptive converse, exact-coefficient qualifications, and reference costs.
- [Whole-register result](learning/MILESTONES.md#m27): M27–M30 connect product structure, the two-versus-three-probe law, and physical resource accounting.

The learning map is independent of individual progress. Explain the science through the linked source and proof pages; do not infer that a reader has passed an assessment or that a finite numerical check proves a universal theorem.

## Definitions and proofs

- [Model](science/model.md): Pure probes, survival loss, Haar risk, and certification access.
- [Robustness](science/robustness.md): Exact Kraus identities; the common right-eigenoperator criterion; optimal linear coefficient; physical sharpness; full exponent trichotomy.
- [Probe geometry](science/probe_geometry.md): Coordinate-support graph, minimal support, explicit qubit obstruction, dimension dependence, and optimized basis-plus-superposition weights.
- [Optimal design](science/optimal_design.md): Universal support-size bound for arbitrary weights and imbalance, ETF equality conditions, and the projective 2-design endpoint.
- [Nonunitality](science/nonunitality.md): Exact commutator identity, sharp unital coefficient, quantitative deviation bound, joint frontier, and dissipative realization.
- [Certification](science/certification.md): Adaptive classical-to-quantum fidelity converse, minimax adversary, finite-sample sandwich, exact joint limiting coefficient, target-copy comparison, and noisy-baseline limits.
- [Product channels](science/product_channels.md): Exact tensor-product promise, uniform two-versus-three global probe laws, sharp coefficients, and physical costs.

## Interpretation constraints

Read the model before transferring a theorem to another access setting. R and R_H denote the same Haar-average infidelity. State fidelity in the certification proof is squared Uhlmann fidelity.

The variance gap is minimized over all traceless complex operators, including nonnormal ones. Restricting it to Hermitian operators removes the relevant dissipative directions.

Exact identification, finite-loss robustness, and statistical certification are different properties. The best global linear coefficient does not determine the full finite-error frontier.

The exact sampling coefficient for a fixed menu holds as both target error and decision error tend to zero, with system dimension fixed and ideal target-output projectors. Fixed-confidence two-sided testing has a bracket; perfect completeness has a sharper coefficient statement.

The adaptive lower bounds allow quantum output memory and collective readout. Each input is fresh and chosen by a classical label; conditional on that label, its preparation is independent of retained memory. The proofs do not grant input entanglement with retained memory, coherent probe choice, output recycling, or environment access.

The product-channel application requires a product-unitary target and exact tensor factorization. Every global example includes all n qubits and local channel uses. Its order bounds are uniform in n, while the exact leading three-probe coefficient is stated at fixed n.

Training-loss estimates used to select a hypothesis are not automatically valid fresh certification data. Finite numerical checks corroborate constructions; they do not prove universal theorems or literature priority.
